subject: MAP: unit economics checkpoints and eval close timeline
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 2 May 2028 14:15 -0700
Subject: MAP: unit economics checkpoints & eval timeline

Hi Sarah / Acme team —

Following our product demo, attached is a first-pass MAP + unit-econ workbook aimed at making the evaluation and close timeline concrete. High level ask: we want alignment on the cost gating checks that must be satisfied before a pilot-to-production commit. Quick summary of the cost assumptions inside the MAP:

- Tokens / session: baseline 1,200 tokens (avg), 95th 6,000 tokens for heavy flows.
- Tokens / $ (hosted): modeled at 0.0000125 $/token for the base LLM variant (this is blended across prompt + generated tokens).
- Caching assumptions: prefix KV cache estimated 35% hit-rate for conversational re-use (will reduce effective tokens/$). Cache only for non-sensitive prefixes — we treat PII as non-cacheable by default.
- Batching: default continuous batching with max_batch_size=32, target latency P95 < 220ms for short sequences; can scale to max_batch_size=64 for throughput tests.
- Fallback policy: MAP proposes automatic fallback to a smaller quantized model once monthly spend hits the agreed cost cap.

What I need from you this week: signoff on these gating numbers (tokens/session and cache hit-rate), confirmation of any regulatory constraints on caching, and a short procurement checklist so we can time the SOW. Proposed MAP timeline:

- Week 0 (May 8): Finalize MAP and SOW items
- Week 1 (May 15): Start eval (smoke tests + quality probes)
- Week 3 (June 5): Canary with 1k users/day or equivalent traffic window
- Week 5 (June 19): MAP close + production handover

I've attached: MAP-draft-Acme-v2.pdf, token-econ-smoke.xlsx (modeling), eval-prompts.json (sample eval prompts).

If it helps, we can add a hard cost-cap gate (monthly token budget) and an automatic rollback plan to keep the pilot within predictable spend — recommended for procurement comfort.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP-draft-Acme-v2.pdf (PDF), token-econ-smoke.xlsx (spreadsheet), eval-prompts.json (json)

From: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 09:30 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: unit economics checkpoints & eval timeline

Karthik —

Thanks for the summary and the attachments. A few clarifying questions before we route to procurement:

1) Tokens/session: our users have a long-tailed distribution (many short lookups, some long multimodal dialogs). Can you provide a 25/50/75/95 token-per-session breakdown so we can map to our traffic?
2) Caching: what exactly is stored in the KV cache, where is it kept, and how long is TTL? We need to confirm no persistent storage of PII.
3) Batching: what are latency implications for interactive users at the P95 if you enable max_batch_size 64? We are sensitive to latency > 250ms.
4) Procurement: we will need SOC2 evidence and your standard data processing addendum. Can you attach the compliance pack?

Also we'd like to see any smoke-test telemetry you have for a similar healthcare customer — especially tokens/$ measured during a 48-hour soak.

Can we do a quick 30-min sync Mon morning to align on the MAP and procurement checklist?

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Kim
Product Manager, Acme Health

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Kim <sarah.kim@acme.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 May 2028 11:45 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: unit economics checkpoints & eval timeline

Sarah — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and actions below.

1) Token distribution (25/50/75/95): 120 / 450 / 1,430 / 6,200. I'll add these percentiles to the MAP workbook (tab "session_dist").

2) Cache mechanics: we use an in-memory KV cache colocated with the inference shards. Cache keys are deterministic prefixes (no user PII in keys unless you opt in). Default TTL is 10 minutes for conversational contexts; configurable per-route. Cache storage is ephemeral and does not persist to disk — we can include a short appendix for your security team.

3) Batching & latency: with max_batch_size 64 you will see throughput gains, but P95 latency for short (<= 512 tokens total) sequences can increase ~60–80ms on our bench. With target max_batch_size 32 we routinely hold P95 < 220ms. MAP recommends starting the eval at max_batch_size 32 and running a throughput window at 64 for the canary to measure degradation.

4) Compliance pack & SOC2: attaching a redacted pack in the Drive link; I'll also loop in our Security contact if you want a call.

Attached now: token-econ-smoke.xlsx (short soak telemetry against a healthcare-like prompt profile). Highlights: effective tokens/$ improves ~28% with a 35% cache hit and batching at 32; latency increases are minimal at that operating point.

Proposal: add a cost-gate row in the MAP with two thresholds:
- Soft gate: warn at 70% of monthly token budget and throttle non-critical flows
- Hard gate: switch to smaller quantized model and pause non-essential features at 100% budget

If that sounds reasonable I'll update MAP-draft-Acme-v2.pdf and send the SOW checklist. 30-min sync Monday 9:00am PT works for me — inviting Laura to cover eval acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Karthik

Attachments: token-econ-smoke.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 4 May 2028 08:10 -0700
Subject: RE: MAP: unit economics checkpoints & eval timeline

Adding internal notes on the eval plan & acceptance criteria (for MAP):

- Quality gates: automated eval pass-rate >= 85% on a stratified prompt set (from eval-prompts.json) and no regression > 5% vs baseline in human-rated quality checks.
- Performance gates: P95 latency <= 220ms (interactive flows) and tokens/$ improvement >= 20% vs unfavorably cached baseline during a 72-hour soak.
- Operational gates: observability hooks enabled (trace id per request), error budget < 1% 5xx over canary window.
- Rollout policy: 20% traffic canary after smoke tests, expand to 60% if gates met for 48 hours.

Related: I've created a HubSpot note for the MAP and linked the MAP draft here: https://hubspot.example/records/DEAL-ACME-023. Please ensure the SOW includes the cost-cap and rollback triggers Laura notes above.

I'll be at the Monday sync to walk acceptance criteria; Rishi can defend the fallback quantization impact on quality.

-Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference

Procurement here. We reviewed the outline and can start the SOW process. Two requests before we issue a PO:

2) Redlined DPA + SOC2 evidence (or link to a SOC2 report we can use under NDA).

We are targeting a 30-day procurement window once the SOW is accepted. Please send a calendar invite for the Monday 9:00am PT sync and include the SOW template if you have one.
